def correct_bracketing(brackets: str):
    
    depth = 0
    for b in brackets:
        if b == "(":
            depth += 1
        else:
            depth -= 1
        if depth < 0:
            return False
    return depth == 0



# Unit test for function correct_bracketing
def test_correct_bracketing():
    # Balanced cases
    assert correct_bracketing("") == True          # empty string is balanced
    assert correct_bracketing("()") == True        # simple pair
    assert correct_bracketing("(())") == True      # nested pair
    assert correct_bracketing("(()())") == True    # nested sequence
    assert correct_bracketing("((()))") == True    # deep nesting
    assert correct_bracketing("()()()") == True    # multiple pairs
    assert correct_bracketing("(())(())()") == True  # mixed nesting

    # Unbalanced cases
    assert correct_bracketing("(") == False        # unclosed bracket
    assert correct_bracketing(")") == False        # unmatched closing
    assert correct_bracketing(")(") == False       # closing before opening
    assert correct_bracketing("(()") == False      # missing closing
    assert correct_bracketing("())") == False      # extra closing
    assert correct_bracketing("(()))(") == False   # goes negative mid-string

    print("All tests passed!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_correct_bracketing()
